literal_current_supplier_used_clauses: For an endpoint bookkeeping quantity $F$, write $\Delta F=F_P^+-F_P^-$. A closed record in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] has no matter crossing the chosen outer boundary throughout $I_P$; zero net matter transfer alone does not suffice. The core closed-record class $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\subseteq\mathcal P_s$ ([[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]) consists exactly of the closed records $P\in\mathcal P_s$ for which the system has a supplied fixed total mass $M>0$ and defined center-of-mass velocities at both endpoints in the fixed chart $g_s$, and $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$. Here $K_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm\|_2^2$ are defined as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], and $U_{\mathrm{ext}}^\pm$ are supplied endpoint values of any model-specified external-field potential energy tracked separately from the internal-energy coordinate in $g_s$; if no such term is tracked, both values are set to zero. Other process classes require an expanded energy bookkeeping rule.

Define $Q:\mathcal P_s\to\mathbb R$ by $Q[P]:=H_P^{\mathrm{in}}(t_1)-H_P^{\mathrm{out}}(t_1)$. The protocol also supplies $W_{\mathrm{on}}:\mathcal P_s\to\mathbb R$, with values in joules; both transfers use the fixed bookkeeping chart $g_s$. Thus $Q[P]>0$ means net thermal energy enters the system, and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]>0$ means net mechanical work is done on it. These are functionals of the process record, not state functions of $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$. A record $P\in\mathcal P_s$ is adiabatic exactly when $H_P^{\mathrm{in}}(t)=H_P^{\mathrm{out}}(t)=0$ for every $t\in I_P$: no thermal energy crosses the selected boundary throughout the record. In particular an adiabatic record has $Q[P]=0$, but zero net heat alone does not specify an adiabatic record. On $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$, use the restrictions of these same maps; defining them on the larger class supplies no energy-balance law for records outside the core class. A closed record may still exchange energy; it is not thereby isolated.
